items.title: Show HN: I made a Raspberry with Qwen my local car AI
items.why: It demonstrates a creative, practical project where AI models run on budget hardware to interact with real-world sensor data.
items.summary: A developer successfully ran a 35-billion parameter Qwen language model on a Raspberry Pi, connecting it to a car's onboard diagnostics port to act as an offline automotive assistant.

items.title: missuo/herdrm
items.why: This tool helps you organize and control multiple command-line AI coding assistants from one central dashboard.
items.summary: Herdrm provides a native macOS terminal application that lets you manage, view, and interact with multiple active AI coding agents simultaneously across devices.

items.title: GamePhanes/GamePhanes
items.why: It is an interesting open-source project combining AI agent development with game creation in the Godot engine.
items.summary: GamePhanes is an open-source framework designed to train and benchmark AI agents as they generate code for the popular Godot game engine.

items.title: Show HN: LatticeDB – Like SQLite but for graph databases
items.why: As a computer science student, learning about lightweight embedded databases gives you valuable software architecture ideas for personal projects.
items.summary: LatticeDB is an open-source embedded graph database designed to be simple to set up locally, similar to how SQLite works for relational databases.

items.title: I were 17, I'd learn how to build LLMs from scratch
items.why: This perspective from Y Combinator founder Paul Graham offers inspiring direction for aspiring CS students entering the AI era.
items.summary: Paul Graham argues that young programmers should focus on building foundational Large Language Models from first principles rather than just relying on high-level API wrappers.

items.title: OpenAI Jalapeño: Better than Nvidia Blackwell
items.why: It covers a significant shift in AI hardware as major AI labs attempt to reduce reliance on Nvidia GPUs.
items.summary: OpenAI is testing custom silicon chips codenamed Jalapeño, claiming in early benchmarks that they can outperform Nvidia's flagship AI processors.

items.title: Python's pre-declared constants are kinda weird
items.why: Understanding the nuances of Python's built-in behaviors helps you write cleaner code and avoid subtle bugs as you learn.
items.summary: This article explores how Python handles pre-declared internal constants like True, False, and None under the hood, pointing out unusual quirks in language implementation.

items.title: CIA chief travels to Moscow for unannounced talks, US media reports
items.why: It keeps you informed on major top-tier diplomatic developments occurring between global superpowers.
items.summary: Flight records and news reports indicate the director of the CIA made an unannounced diplomatic visit to Moscow for high-level talks amid international tensions.

items.title: Seven killed in Gaza as Israeli strike ‘destroys’ aid supply warehouse
items.why: It provides crucial coverage on major international events and ongoing global conflicts.
items.summary: An airstrike destroyed a critical humanitarian aid supply warehouse in Gaza, escalating warnings of a severe breakdown in essential human supplies.

items.title: Brazil fines TikTok $30m for child data privacy violations
items.why: It highlights global legal efforts to regulate tech giants over user privacy and child safety.
items.summary: Brazilian regulators fined TikTok $30 million and ordered the deletion of illegally collected data belonging to underage users.
